items.body:
##### SUMMARY
When gathering facts for Debian systems, Ansible fails to detect at least "bullseye". The fact "ansible_distribution_release" is "NA". 
This seems to be caused by trying to call a shell-command via module.run_command(), but not specifying "use_unsafe_shell=True"

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
module_utils/facts/system/distribution.py

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
```paste below
2.9.9
```
but seems to still be the same on master as well.

##### CONFIGURATION
```paste below
ALLOW_WORLD_READABLE_TMPFILES(/opt/svn/Ansible/ansible.cfg) = True
ANSIBLE_PIPELINING(/opt/svn/Ansible/ansible.cfg) = True
ANSIBLE_SSH_ARGS(/opt/svn/Ansible/ansible.cfg) = -C -o ControlMaster=no -o ControlPersist=15m
DEFAULT_GATHERING(/opt/svn/Ansible/ansible.cfg) = smart
DEFAULT_GATHER_SUBSET(/opt/svn/Ansible/ansible.cfg) = [u'min']
DEFAULT_SCP_IF_SSH(/opt/svn/Ansible/ansible.cfg) = True
DEFAULT_STDOUT_CALLBACK(/opt/svn/Ansible/ansible.cfg) = debug
```

##### OS / ENVIRONMENT
Host: Ubuntu 18.04
Remote system: Debian Bullseye


##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE
Run `ansible -m setup` against a Debian Bullseye operating system and check `ansible_distribution_release`. It will be "NA".

##### EXPECTED RESULTS
It should properly detect this as `ansible_distribution_release: "bullseye"`.


##### ACTUAL RESULTS
The reason for this is that at https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/stable-2.9/lib/ansible/module_utils/facts/system/distribution.py#L314 the call to `module.run_command` tries to run a shell command (it tries to pipe the output into other commands!), but does not specify `use_unsafe_shell=True`.

There is actually an error reported by run_command here, something along "Error: --status requires a valid package name", which is from dpkg because it recieves the whole commandline including the piped commands as it's argument. 

See https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/module_utils/basic.py#L2424 for the description of this argument of `run_command`.

Adding `use_unsafe_shell=True` locally makes it work, but the proper fix may be different if you want to avoid invoking the shell here.

Ideally there should be some better error-handling here to actually show this in debug-output as it was not visible even with -vvv and thus was quite hard to narrow down!
